result:
I'd make people genuinely curious about perspectives radically different from their own—not to convince them, but just to actually *understand* how someone else's world makes sense to them.

Most conflict seems to come from people being certain they understand why others believe what they do, when usually they've just built a caricature. A real shift in that—where curiosity felt as natural and satisfying as certainty does now—might unwind a lot of knots.

It's not optimistic exactly. People might understand each other better and *still* choose opposition. But at least it'd be honest opposition, not opposition built on strawmen.
